item.title: Folorunsho Alakija Conferred With Honorary Doctorate By UK’s Buckingham University
item.description: Prominent businesswoman, philanthropist and Christian minister, Apostle Folorunso Alakija, has been conferred with an honorary doctorate by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom. The honour was presented at a ceremony on Friday, in recognition of her achievements in business and contributions to society. Businesswoman, philanthropist and Christian minister, Apostle Folorunso Alakija, was conferred with an honorary doctorate by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom on Friday, October 16, 2026. Alakija’s career spans banking, fashion, oil and gas, real estate and philanthropy, establishing her as one of Africa’s most prominent business figures. Beyond her commercial interests, she has supported charitable initiatives focused on education, women’s empowerment and vulnerable communities. Alakija and others at the honorary doctorate conferment by the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom on Friday, October 16, 2026. The ceremony brought together university officials and guests to celebrate her achievements and contributions to enterprise and philanthropy. item.description: African passports differ significantly in the number of destinations their holders can visit without obtaining a visa before departure, with Seychelles, Mauritius and South Africa leading the continent in international travel access. The Henley Passport Index, which uses data from the International Air Transport Association (IATA), ranks passports according to the number of destinations their holders can access without a prior visa. Its 2026 rankings place Seychelles among Africa’s strongest passports, followed by Mauritius and South Africa. Based on the 2026 rankings and available passport-mobility data, here are five African countries whose passports offer extensive international travel access. Seychelles Seychelles has one of Africa’s most powerful passports, giving its citizens broad access to destinations across the world without securing a visa in advance. The island nation retained its position as Africa’s leading passport in the 2026 Henley Passport Index, ranking among the top 25 passports globally in the July update. According to the Seychelles News Agency, the passport provided visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 155 destinations at that time. Its international mobility gives Seychellois citizens greater flexibility when planning holidays, business trips and other short-term journeys abroad. The country’s position reflects the benefits of its international relations and the travel arrangements it has established with other countries. item.title: Buhari offered to support Osinbajo’s presidential bid four times — Akande counters Babachir Lawal
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former spokesperson to ex-Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo, Laolu Akande has dismissed claims by Babachir Lawal that former President Muhammadu Buhari considered Osinbajo’s 2023 presidential ambition “highly immoral and distasteful”. Akande, who served as Osinbajo’s spokesperson from 2015 to 2023, described the allegation as false in a statement on Saturday, saying Buhari had personally offered to support the former vice-president’s ambition on at least four occasions. Osinbajo contested the All Progressives Congress presidential primary in 2022 but lost to Bola Tinubu, who went on to win the 2023 presidential election. Lawal, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, ADC, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, had alleged in a recent interview that Buhari would have found it difficult to support Osinbajo’s ambition because of his longstanding relationship with Tinubu, a former Lagos State governor. Reacting, Akande said he had watched the interview in which Lawal made allegations against Osinbajo and chose to respond because he was present when decisions concerning the former vice-president’s office were taken. He said Buhari had, on at least four separate occasions, personally offered to support Osinbajo, asking him, “If I don’t support you, who will I support?” “He was consistent. During the APC presidential primaries in 2022, while campaigns were underway, President Buhari openly commended Vice President Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for the dignified, issues-based manner in which he was conducting his campaign across the country. He spoke in a laudatory tone. The entire Council witnessed it.” “That is not a President who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a President who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” Akande added. Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022, finishing third with 235 votes, behind now president Bola Tinubu, who won with 1,271 votes, and Rotimi Amaechi, who scored 316. item.title: Tinubu Builds His Coalition. Can The Opposition Build A Contest?
item.description: There is something revealing about the political events of this week. Both sides are pursuing the same objective: assembling enough political strength to win the 2027 presidential election. But they are approaching it from very different positions. And somewhere between those two calculations are millions of Nigerian voters who may have a rather different set of priorities. An APC Campaign Council With An Unusual Guest List Wednesday’s inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council was more than a gathering of party faithful. Among those openly supporting Tinubu were Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo and Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke. Yet all three have publicly committed themselves to Tinubu’s re-election. This is not necessarily a merger of political parties. Nor does it guarantee that their supporters will follow them into the APC’s electoral column. But it demonstrates how the President intends to fight the election: not simply by relying on the APC’s traditional structures, but by recruiting influential political actors wherever they can be found. There is a familiar Nigerian political calculation at work here. A governor may belong to one party, a minister to another, and their supporters may carry several different membership cards. But when an election approaches, the question increasingly becomes who can deliver votes. That is the strength of Tinubu’s approach. It is also its potential weakness. An alliance assembled around personalities can be formidable on election day. Whether it produces lasting political coherence is another matter. Already, questions are being raised about the propriety of politicians campaigning for a presidential candidate outside their own parties. Atiku’s camp has supported calls for judicial clarification of the position. The dispute could become an early test of party discipline, constitutional rights and the increasingly fluid boundaries of Nigerian party politics. The Opposition’s Crowded Negotiating Table There is movement on the other side, too. The ADC, APM, NDC, SDP, PDP and PRP have reportedly held consultations involving five presidential candidates as they explore cooperation ahead of 2027. That is politically significant. But consultation is not consolidation. The opposition must still answer three difficult questions. Who leads? What does each participant gain? And how will supporters be persuaded to transfer their loyalty to a common electoral project? These are not minor details. They are the difference between a coalition that can compete and a coalition that exists mainly in communiqués. Atiku brings extensive political experience and established networks. Obi retains an identifiable reform-oriented following, particularly among younger and urban voters. Makinde has executive experience and a political base in the South-West. Other candidates bring regional relationships and alternative policy perspectives. Combining these strengths could create a more competitive presidential race. But political support is not automatically transferable. An Obi supporter may not necessarily vote for Atiku. A Makinde supporter may not automatically embrace Obi. And some voters attracted to smaller parties may reject any arrangement that appears to reproduce the political establishment they want to replace. The opposition’s challenge, therefore, is not merely to agree on a candidate. It is to create a proposition that voters find credible. For now, the ruling party has an organisational advantage. Whether that translates into electoral victory will depend on what happens between now and January. The Economy: Better Figures, Difficult Conversations Thursday brought some welcome economic news for the government. Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.63 per cent in September, compared with 15.39 per cent in August. For an administration that has defended difficult economic reforms, the figures offer further evidence that inflationary pressures are easing. But there is a complication. Food inflation remains at 19.59 per cent. And the distinction matters enormously. Economists understand that falling inflation means prices are rising more slowly. But the average family shopping in the market is less interested in the rate of increase than in the amount of money required to feed the household. This is where the government’s economic argument meets its political test. Tinubu can point to improving macroeconomic indicators, stronger growth and the prospect of greater stability. His opponents can point to the accumulated burden of high prices, expensive transportation and declining purchasing power. Both arguments may resonate with different sections of the electorate. The latest disagreement between the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress over when negotiations for a new minimum wage should begin adds another dimension. Labour wants talks to start now. The government considers an immediate review premature. That disagreement could become politically consequential if it develops into industrial action. For the APC, the challenge is to demonstrate that economic recovery is reaching households. For the opposition, the challenge is to move beyond criticism and explain how it would reduce hardship without undermining fiscal stability. Neither task is straightforward. Security: A Campaign Cannot Outrun Events While politicians prepare their rallies, the security situation is providing a sobering reminder that elections do not take place in isolation. Reports of an attack on a military base in Mairari, Borno State, with significant casualties among soldiers and civilian security volunteers, have again raised questions about the resilience of security operations in the North-East. The reported casualty figures have not been independently confirmed by the military. On Thursday, Tinubu directed security agencies to intensify operations against terrorists and kidnappers, while preparing a secure environment for the 2027 elections. There is also the continuing anguish surrounding the October 5 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. Reuters reported today that families of some of the 25 people who died are still seeking clear information about the investigation, recovery efforts and support for relatives. These developments raise an uncomfortable political question. How effectively can a government campaign on security improvements when serious incidents continue to expose operational weaknesses? The opposition will undoubtedly make security part of its case against the administration. But it, too, must explain what it would do differently, how it would fund those changes, and how quickly Nigerians could reasonably expect results. item.title: Kwara APC: Oba leads peace committee to reconcile aggrieved members
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, OFR, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group, known as the Kwara APC Peace Committee, held its inaugural meeting at AbdulRaheem’s residence in Ilorin on September 17, according to a statement made available to Vanguard by Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin. The statement said the committee was committed to resolving disagreements arising from the outcome of the APC primaries and promoting unity among party members. AbdulRaheem, a former chairman of the Federal Character Commission, chairs the committee. Other members include Dr Johnson Adewumi, an educationist, entrepreneur and founder of Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former minister and former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to the Kwara State Government and former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo. The committee also comprises Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and Africa representative on the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; former Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and member of the Tinubu-Shettima Presidential Campaign Council, Pastor John Dara; and former Federal Character Commission member, Hon. James Jiya Kolo. According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq. It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections. The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Rt. Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other candidates of the party in the state. The statement said the initiative was aimed at securing the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthening cohesion within the APC ahead of the general elections. item.title: Pope to return to Vatican after cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital Saturday where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”. Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour. “Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican. The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”. “He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment,” the Vatican said. The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square. But in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms. The Vatican’s press office said that Leo celebrated mass on Saturday, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital where he has been recovering. – Up in air – News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics. But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take. Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky. Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. Pope watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors. Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20. The pope himself announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed. item.title: Nigeria commiserates with Saudi Arabia over terrorists’ attacks
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo ‎ ‎President Bola Tinubu has conveyed heartfelt condolences to the government and people of Saudi Arabia over the recent numerous attacks on the country by the Houthi militia from Yemen. ‎ ‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made this known when he received the Ambassador of Saudi Arabia to Nigeria, Yousef bin Mohammed Al-Balawi, in his office during the week. ‎ ‎In the letter, President Tinubu strongly condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia by Houthi militia and commiserated with the Prime Minister, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the government and people of Saudi Arabia on the attacks that have claimed many lives and destroyed physical infrastructure and critical installations in the country. ‎ ‎While delivering the letter to the Ambassador, the Minister noted that there was no alternative to peace, urging people in the region to eschew violence. ‎ ‎An obviously elated Ambassador Yousef expressed profound appreciation to President Tinubu for his kind words of solidarity, consolation and principled stance of strong condemnation and abhorrence of terrorists and rebel activists against legitimate governments while stressing his unalloyed commitment to regional and international peace and security. ‎ ‎The Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communications to the Minister, Mr. Richard Elesho, made this known in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday. item.title: Gunmen storm Plateau community, kill four vigilantes
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed four vigilantes keeping watch over their community in Shurum village, Dorowa Babuje, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 11:56pm on Friday, when the attackers stormed the community and killed the vigilantes while they were on duty. A member of the community, Mr Bulus Bature, said, “They were watching over our community when the gunmen struck and killed them.” Lamenting the killings, Bature said, “It is painful that people who volunteered to protect their community could be attacked and killed while carrying out their duty.” The National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong also confirmed the incident to Vanguard. Tengwong said, “We received information about the attack and can confirm that four people were killed by the gunmen.” He condemned the killings, saying, “It is unfortunate that our people, who were keeping watch over their community, were targeted and killed.” He added, “We are deeply saddened by this latest attack and call on the relevant security agencies to urgently investigate the incident and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.” Tengwong further said, “Our people cannot continue to live in fear while those volunteering to protect their communities are being attacked and killed.” “We appeal to the government and security agencies to strengthen security around the affected communities.” Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of press time. item.title: Everton vs Chelsea: All the talking points
item.description: Chelsea face their first away trip outside London this season when they travel to Merseyside to take on Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in Saturday’s 12:30 p.m. Premier League fixture. The encounter marks Chelsea’s second visit to Everton’s new home, with the Blues eager to bounce back from their previous meeting at the stadium, where they suffered a disappointing 3-0 defeat earlier this year. Chelsea head into the contest in encouraging form following their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth last weekend. The result leaves them with one more win, four additional goals and two more points than they had at the corresponding stage of the previous campaign. The Blues have also developed a habit of scoring early this season, breaking the deadlock five times in the opening stages of their league matches. Their ability to strike quickly could prove valuable against an Everton side that has remained unbeaten so far this term. Everton, meanwhile, drew 2-2 with Hull City on Sunday, scoring the first league goals conceded by the Tigers at home this season. The match presents an intriguing contest between Chelsea’s potent attacking force and Everton’s impressive defensive record. The fixture has featured in every Premier League season since 1989, making it a familiar rivalry for both clubs. Chelsea have enjoyed considerable success in early Saturday kick-offs, remaining unbeaten in their last 10 matches played in the 12:30 p.m. slot, recording eight victories and two draws. Their most recent appearance in that time window ended in a 1-1 draw against Liverpool at Anfield in May. A victory on Saturday would see Chelsea move above Everton in the league standings and could lift them as high as fourth place, depending on the outcome of Brentford’s clash with Liverpool later in the day. Chelsea’s historical struggles at Everton Despite their recent form, Chelsea face a difficult challenge given their record on Everton’s home turf. Only Liverpool, where the Blues have suffered 50 league defeats, have proved a more troublesome away destination than Everton, against whom Chelsea have lost 44 times—the same number as against Arsenal. Goodison Park hosted most of those defeats, accounting for 43 of them. Their most recent victory at Goodison Park came in August 2022, when Jorginho converted a penalty to secure the points and end a run of four consecutive defeats at the ground. Chelsea’s history at Everton stretches back more than a century. Their first league victory at Goodison came in April 1908, when George Hilsdon scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 triumph. The Blues also recorded a memorable 3-2 victory on Merseyside in August 1919, shortly after the resumption of football following the First World War. They repeated the scoreline three years later, although another 26 years passed before they claimed all three points there again, with Roy Bentley scoring in another 3-2 win. Further memorable successes followed, including a 2-0 win in March 1969, courtesy of goals from Alan Birchenall and Ian Hutchinson. item.title: Oil tanker on fire after hitting mine in Hormuz – Iran’s Guards
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Saturday said an oil tanker was on fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting a mine in the waterway at the heart of the Middle East war. Tehran seized control over Hormuz after the start of the war in late February, choking off the strait that normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption. “A supertanker in violation of regulations, carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and attempting to pass illegally through the Strait of Hormuz, struck a mine, triggering an explosion and a fierce fire,” the Revolutionary Guards said. The statement did not specify the exact location of the incident. Flanked by Iran to the north and Oman to the south, the Hormuz strait is about 30 kilometres (20 miles) wide at its narrowest point. Since taking control of the strait, Iran has demanded that all ships seek its authorisation before transiting. “The tanker attempted to cross the strait with US support… by deactivating all its tracking systems,” the Guards added, also posting a video of a vessel in flames during the night. In response to Tehran’s blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, Washington has imposed its own naval counter-blockade on Iranian oil exports. This week, the Guards’ naval commander Admiral Ali Ozmai warned that any vessel that deactivated its navigation systems would be considered “hostile”. item.title: DSS Arrests Maina’s Son In Abuja
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has arrested Faisal Abdulrasheed Maina, fugitive son of the former Chairman of the defunct Pension Reform Task Team, Abdulrasheed Maina. The agency has also handed him over to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Security sources revealed that Faisal, who has been on the run since 2020, was trailed and apprehended by operatives of the DSS in the Karsana area of Abuja. “His arrest followed credible intelligence which indicated that Faisal had secretly returned to the country”, a source revealed. It will be recalled that Faisal was prosecuted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on a three-count charge bordering on money laundering and conspiracy. He subsequently violated his bail conditions and escaped the country. The trial continued in his absence, culminating in his conviction and sentence to 14 years’ imprisonment by Justice Okon Abang in 2021. The Court had ordered that Faisal be arrested wherever he was found in Nigeria and remanded in a correctional centre to serve his sentence. It further directed that, if found outside the country, the Federal Government should take lawful steps to secure his extradition to serve his prison term. “The handover of Faisal to the EFCC is expected to facilitate the enforcement of the Court’s judgment and ensure that he serves his sentence in accordance with the law”, a source declared. item.title: Bauchi court jails eight for eight years over public disturbance
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi A Bauchi State court has sentenced eight persons to eight years’ imprisonment each for thuggery and disturbance of public peace in Unguwar Dim, Bauchi metropolis. The convicts were also given the option of a N370,000 fine each, the Bauchi State Police Command has said. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Saturday, saying the suspects were arrested following a complaint by the Unguwar Dim Peace and Security Committee on October 14 over renewed thuggery in the area. Habib said a joint team of police operatives and community security personnel raided the suspects’ hideout in the early hours of October 15, arresting nine persons. Dangerous weapons, including machetes, cutlasses, knives and sticks, as well as illicit substances, were recovered during the operation, he added. According to him, eight suspects were charged to court after investigations and convicted after pleading guilty to the charges. The Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, welcomed the judgment and urged residents to provide credible information to assist the police in tackling criminal activities. Aliyu reaffirmed the command’s commitment to combating thuggery and other crimes, assuring residents of sustained operations to safeguard lives and property across the state. item.title: Anthropic proposes law regulating AI to US lawmakers
item.description: Anthropic, the creator of the AI assistant Claude, confirmed on Friday it is circulating a draft bill among US lawmakers aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to address the lack of federal legislation on the risks posed by the new technology. According to the draft, first reported by Politico on Friday, Washington could block a model’s release or use if there is an imminent risk of killing or seriously injuring more than 50 people, or causing more than $1 billion in damages, but only with a judge’s approval. A company spokesperson told AFP that the proposal “grants the federal government the ability to block or deter dangerous deployments of the most powerful models.” “It requires frontier developers to test the most powerful models, be transparent to the public about their findings, submit them to independent evaluation, and maintain a robust security program,” the spokesperson said. AI policy in the United States under President Donald Trump has relied primarily on voluntary industry pledges and executive orders intended to sustain an AI boom that tech leaders say is driving the country’s economy. Congress, politically divided and heavily lobbied by Big Tech, has yet to pass a federal AI law, and is out of session until after next month’s midterm elections. Security became a hot topic after recent revelations of security incidents caused by AI agents — autonomous software that operates without constant human supervision — that escaped the control of their developers. Anthropic, which was banned from the Pentagon by the Trump administration in February, was forced by Washington in June to suspend its most advanced models for nearly three weeks. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on the industry last month to slow down development, fearing that a group of AI agents could take control of “the entire internet” within six to 12 months. Trump has dismissed the numerous calls to slow down the technology as “negative forces.” The proposed legislation would also override certain state laws, such as those in force in California. Anthropic wrote in June that “absent a strong federal law, states should retain full authority to legislate.” Charlie Bullock of the Institute for Law & AI think tank praised the proposal as “pretty reasonable,” and “more than other frontier labs have done.” But he said on X he considers it “weaker” than the FRONTIER Act, a competing bill introduced in the House of Representatives this summer. item.title: Trump signs executive order waiving new Russia sanctions, tariffs
item.description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia’s energy revenues after signing them into law last month. The Lindsey Graham Act — named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill — allowed Trump the authority to impose duties up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. “As described further in section 4 of this order, I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act,” the executive order said. The law targeted Russia’s energy and defense sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials, as well as Moscow’s so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent Western sanctions. Trump’s reversal on the Russia sanctions comes in after a controversial deal he struck with Putin that would allow Russia diesel exports in exchange for US sanctions relief. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since the deal, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky calling it a “weak decision” and Ukrainian forces resuming attacks on Russian oil refineries. For many young people, it intersects with unemployment, economic pressure, trauma, peer influence, family stress and social exclusion. A young person’s encounter with the justice system, he showed, can become either a revolving door of arrest, release and repeat offending or a turning point towards assessment, treatment and recovery. He challenged the country to rethink its response to youth drug addiction and the intersection between substance use disorders and the criminal justice system. In his presentation, Ikpechukwu posed a question that went to the heart of the debate: “Which pathway better protects the young person, the family and society?” His argument was not that drug-related offences should be excused or that addiction should become a blanket defence against criminal responsibility. Rather, he called for a response that recognises the distinction between criminal accountability and the treatment of a health condition. “Not excusing crime. Not criminalising illness. Not abandoning accountability,” Ikpeachukwu stressed in framing the purpose of a more effective response. item.title: DSS, military, police arrest 5 over NYSC members kidnap
item.description: …As 3 others escape with gunshot injuries By Soni Daniel Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), the military and police have arrested five suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly responsible for the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo State on Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day. Five other suspected members of the gang, however, escaped with gunshot injuries prompting a massive manhunt for them. The suspects were apprehended during a series of intelligence-led operations conducted at different locations in Rivers and Abia States. However, in the course of the operation, three other suspects escaped with varying degrees of injury. Security sources disclosed that the operations were carried out between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State and Aba South LGA. Abia State. Recall that 20 NYSC members were abducted by armed men along Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, as they travelled to their assigned orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The victims were subsequently rescued on October 7, 2026, during a joint security operation at Amakohia Ubi Village. The string of operations mark a significant breakthrough in efforts to track down the perpetrators, dismantle the criminal network allegedly responsible for the abduction and bring those involved to justice. A security source described the development as a major relief, noting that security agencies had sustained a wide-ranging manhunt for the abductors. “This is a huge sigh of relief. Security agencies have been on a manhunt for the abductors, and we are elated that they have been captured. We strongly believe they will be charged to Court by DSS and the corps members will get justice,” the source said. item.title: NFF Normalisation Committee: FIFA keeps Nigeria waiting
item.description: The Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) is still awaiting clarification from FIFA following Thursday’s FIFA Council meeting in Zurich, Switzerland, amid expectations that the country’s football leadership crisis would be on the front burner. The FIFA Council held its 37th meeting on October 15, 2026, with discussions covering football development funding, governance reforms and disciplinary procedures. However, FIFA’s published statement on the meeting did not confirm whether the Council approved the proposed Normalisation Committee for Nigeria. The absence of a public announcement does not necessarily mean Nigeria’s situation was not discussed behind closed doors. Among the key developments, FIFA announced plans to increase football development investment to US$6.35 billion for the 2027–2030 cycle, covering its 211 member associations, confederations and other stakeholders. The proposed framework could allow individual member associations to receive allocations of up to US$25 million, subject to applicable requirements and approval procedures. The Council also agreed to establish a working group to examine FIFA’s governance framework and directed relevant committees to review disciplinary procedures. The meeting attracted particular interest in Nigeria following the August resignations of former NFF President Ibrahim Gusau, General Secretary Mohammed Sanusi and members of the federation’s executive board. A joint FIFA and Confederation of African Football (CAF) delegation subsequently visited Nigeria in September to consult stakeholders and examine possible solutions to the crisis. One option reportedly under consideration is a Normalisation Committee to manage the federation temporarily, implement reforms and organise elections. Earlier reports indicated that the matter could be considered under the FIFA Council’s miscellaneous agenda. On Thursday October 15, Nigerian football stakeholders waited in vain for official clarification on whether FIFA will constitute a Normalisation Committee and issue a timetable for restoring elected leadership.
